task: Widen hosted-app sharing operations (share, unshare, shared-with, people search, share-link get/create/revoke, single-grant delete, can_share) from creator-only to every hosted-app manager while assistants keep the owner rule, with manager-named refusals and updated API baseline and design records (EPMCDME-17239).

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the hosted catalog gate (seven sharing entry points), hosted grant and share-link descriptors, projections (can_share), core access rules, and the generic named-grant / share-link / permission-deletion services shared with assistants; the owner rule is enforced twice (catalog and generic descriptor check) so both must change while assistant descriptors stay untouched.

Authorization widening. Closest pattern is the existing SQL manager rule (access.manageable) and Ability WRITE, which covers who manages but not sharing-specific behaviours: no Python manager predicate twin, no mechanism to refuse granting to the creator or to exclude the creator from people search, and orphan-grant handling for single-grant delete must be decided when D9 replaces grant_remover. Edge cases (suspended app, 403 vs 404, creator recipient) are covered by existing persona-table test templates, so no extra bump.

About 10 source files across core/service/router, two design docs, the OpenAPI baseline (7 descriptions), and many owner-centric tests whose assertions flip (catalog, projections, access, share-link service, deletion service, PG matrix, router), plus new tests for creator exclusion — 11-15+ files across multiple subsystems.
AC1-AC8 and D9 are concrete; open points are orphan-grant delete handling and the people-search statement contradicted by the backend (no current exclusion).

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: affects authorization (who may share, revoke links and delete grants)
